gn.en.gn.be-statements.note: Use am, is, and are to say who or what something is: I am ready, the shop is open, we are here. 'Be' changes with the subject — I am, he or she is, you and we and they are.
gn.en.gn.be-statements.title: Statements with 'be'
gn.en.gn.plural-nouns.note: Most English nouns add -s for more than one: cup and cups, name and names. A few common nouns change instead, like person and people.
gn.en.gn.plural-nouns.title: Plural nouns with -s
gn.en.gn.present-simple-12p.note: For habits and facts, use the base verb with I, you, we, and they: I smile, you want, we drink. No ending is added for these subjects — the verb stays in its plain form.
gn.en.gn.present-simple-12p.title: Present simple: I / you / we / they
ovl.es.en.gn.be-statements.note: Spanish splits 'to be' into ser and estar; English uses one verb for both. Say the shop is open (estar sense) and the shop is small (ser sense) with the same 'is'.
